title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Industry Code Penalties) Bill 2014
short_title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Industry Code Penalties) Bill 2014

speeches.speaker: Bruce Billson
speeches.brief: Introduced a bill enabling civil penalties of up to 300 penalty units, currently $51,000, for breaches of the Franchising Code of Conduct, following a 2013 review by Alan Wein, and noted the sector comprises around 73,000 units employing over 400,000 Australians with more than $131 billion in annual sales turnover.

speeches.speaker: Bernie Ripoll
speeches.brief: Supported the Competition and Consumer Amendment (Industry Code Penalties) Bill 2014 introducing pecuniary penalties of up to $51,000 for breaches of the franchising code, based on the Wein review, and noted about 73,000 franchisees contribute more than $130 billion annually to the economy.

speeches.speaker: Philip Ruddock
speeches.brief: Declared that the Competition and Consumer Amendment (Industry Code Penalties) Bill 2014, the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment Bill 2014, and the International Tax Agreements Amendment Bill 2014 were referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

speeches.speaker: Peter Hendy
speeches.brief: Supported the Competition and Consumer Amendment (Industry Code Penalties) Bill 2014, saying it would enable civil penalties and infringement notices under a new franchising code, strengthen enforcement, promote good faith and support small business.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: Supported the Competition and Consumer Amendment (Industry Code Penalties) Bill, noting the franchising sector employs over 400,000 Australians across 73,000 business units, and said no opposition member had spoken on the bill.

speeches.speaker: Fiona Scott
speeches.brief: Supported the Competition and Consumer Amendment (Industry Code Penalties) Bill 2014, describing reforms to modernise franchising regulation, improve disclosure and enforcement, reduce disputes and set penalties of 300 penalty units, 50 penalty units and 10 penalty units.

speeches.speaker: Ewen Jones
speeches.brief: Supported the franchising code penalties bill, saying it would allow pecuniary penalties of up to 300 penalty units, or $51,000, for breaches, and cited over 11,000 small businesses in his Herbert electorate.

speeches.speaker: Steve Irons
speeches.brief: Supported the franchising code penalties bill, describing how five of 16 Western Australian franchisees of Michel's Patisserie faced financial ruin after being sold a flawed business model, and said the bill would give the ACCC power to issue infringement notices and pecuniary penalties for breaches.

speeches.speaker: Jane Prentice
speeches.brief: Supported the franchising code penalties bill responding to the 2013 Wein review, noting her Ryan electorate has more than 1,200 small businesses, and quoted the Law Council of Australia's argument that penalties would deter code breaches and address an imbalance of power between franchisors and franchisees.

acts.title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Industry Code Penalties) Act 2014
